title: Introduce step-orchestrator slim quickstart: checkpointed RAG steps and minimal tool binding
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: a compact, production-minded quickstart that demonstrates how to author a stepwise RAG orchestrator which checkpoints progress at the step level, supports partial-response resume, and binds lightweight tools (search indexer, extractor) with minimal scaffolding. This PR adds a slim starter that focuses on: 1) a tiny step-orchestrator runtime (TypeScript) that executes deterministic step sequences with explicit step state and checkpoint serialization, 2) an embeddable local indexer adapter (SQLite-backed) for low-friction retrieval while developing offline, 3) step probes for telemetry (per-step latency, token-cost tags) wired to the quickstart test harness, and 4) straightforward examples showing tool fallback and canary step rollouts. Changeset summary: commits implement the orchestrator runner, add two example recipes (faq-compile and multi-tool-entity-extraction), provide a devcontainers + small CI smoke workflow, and update the docs site quickstarts index with a modular entry. Checklist: - [x] Add orchestrator runtime and step contract definitions - [x] Add SQLite-based local indexer adapter with seed script - [x] Add sample step recipes and test harness - [x] Add lightweight telemetry probes and example dashboards links - [x] Add devcontainer and CI smoke job - [x] Docs site entry and quickstart README Usage notes: The quickstart is intended to be runnable with only Docker and Node 18. Local bootstrap uses the included seed_index.sh to create a compact SQLite vector index. Run steps with yarn start:quickstart. It demonstrates resume via ./scripts/resume_step.sh which rehydrates step state and resumes an interrupted session. Security notes: the local indexer adapter is intentionally simple and not for production; we include a migration pointer to Redwood's indexer adapter API for customers.
